```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4)
```

A confirmatory trial has one pre-specified mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM). mmrmstress refits it under
families of perturbations of the modelling decisions and the data, judges every refit against the pre-specified
estimate, confidence interval and significance level, and classifies the result as robust, sensitive or fragile.

## The pre-specified analysis

Describe the analysis once. The example uses the `fev_data` set that ships with mmrm, restricted to 100 subjects so the
vignette builds quickly.

```{r spec}
library(mmrmstress)
dat <- mmrm::fev_data[mmrm::fev_data$USUBJID %in% paste0("PT", 1:100), ]
spec <- stress_spec(dat, response = "FEV1", subject = "USUBJID", visit = "AVISIT",
                    treatment = "ARMCD", reference = "PBO", covariates = ~ RACE + SEX + FEV1_BL,
                    contrast_visit = "VIS4", covariance = "us",
                    method = "Satterthwaite", vcov = "Asymptotic")
spec
stress_fit(spec)
```

If you already have an `mmrm` fit, `stress_spec_mmrm(fit, reference = "PBO")` builds the same object; from an ADaM BDS
data set, `stress_spec_adam()` does.

## Families

Each family function returns rows in one schema. A few of them:

```{r families}
stress_covariance(spec, c("us", "cs", "ar1h"))[, c("label", "estimate", "stderr", "p", "is_base")]
stress_inference(spec)[, c("label", "estimate", "stderr", "df", "p")]
stress_covariates(spec)[, c("label", "estimate", "p")]
```

Deletions, re-randomisation, reference-based and delta-adjusted multiple imputation, other estimators, a greedy
search for the smallest set of subjects that changes the conclusion, intercurrent-event strategies and continuous
perturbation curves are the other families; see the reference index.

## Census, verdict and figures

```{r census}
cen <- stress_census(spec, stress_covariance(spec, c("us", "cs", "ar1h")), stress_inference(spec),
                     stress_covariates(spec), stress_loo(spec, by = "RACE"))
summary(cen)
stress_verdict(cen)
plot_swarm(cen)
```

## Pre-specify and run in one call

A plan fixes the families and their settings before unblinding; printing it gives the text a statistical analysis plan
can carry. `standard_plan()` is the recommended set.

```{r plan}
plan <- stress_plan(spec, covariance = list(structures = c("us", "cs", "ar1h")), inference = list(),
                    covariates = list(), weights = TRUE, loo = list(by = "RACE"), permute = list(n = 99),
                    reference = NULL, estimator = list(estimators = c("complete_cases", "ancova")),
                    fragility = list(max_k = 2))
plan
res <- run_plan(plan, seed = 1)
res
```

`stress_report()` writes a Markdown report with the figures, `stress_tables()` the Word or RTF tables and the census
as CSV, `stress_html()` an interactive page, and `stress_log()` the audit trail with the plan's hash.
